question: Does adding full lsp provide enough incremental value for luna-code on a real cross-file TypeScript dependency-navigation task?

decision.scope: default full lsp capability for luna-code based on Phase B2
decision.summary: The treatment naturally made zero LSP calls, produced the same correct dependency map as the baseline, added prompt overhead, and used more wall/model time, tokens and cost. Lower read/grep/tool counts cannot be attributed to LSP because it was unused.

task.constraint: read-only dependency map; no product decision

controlledVariables: independent dependency installations from one lockfile
fresh sessions and no cross-run answer contamination

limitations: One stochastic A/B pair on one repository and one dependency-navigation task.
The treatment did not call lsp, so no quality or efficiency difference can be attributed to semantic navigation.
Exact JSON tool-schema bytes were not measured; only the rendered system-prompt delta is known.
The decision rejects default exposure from this B2 evidence and does not claim LSP is useless on every coding task.
Main's independent ground truth used exact symbol search and bounded source/test reads because the Main LSP device had no server for the external checkout.
